<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Armed conflict and attacks
*[[2019 Sri Lanka Easter bombings]]
**A series of explosions at churches and hotels in four cities in [[Sri Lanka]], including the nation's commercial capital and largest city  [[Colombo]], kills at least 300 people and wounds around 500. Sri Lankan officials claim that no specific group has claimed responsibility but are saying that the work is that of [[Islamic extremists]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-48008073 (BBC)] 
**The Sri Lankan government temporarily [[Censorship in South Asia#Sri Lanka|blocks access]] to all social media platforms to stop the spread of "false media reports" about the attacks.  [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2019/04/21/sri-lankan-government-blocks-social-media-imposes-curfew-following-deadly-blasts/ (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[United States Secretary of State|U.S. Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] has stated that several United States citizens were killed in the attacks and Sri Lanka's Foreign Ministry officials have stated that at least five of the victims were of British nationality. [https://www.cnn.com/asia/live-news/sri-lanka-easter-sunday-explosions-dle-intl/h_7cf075d83c893b55b334e94892ffb15c (CNN)]
*Four attackers are killed in a failed attack in [[Riyadh]], [[Saudi Arabia]]. The attackers had machine guns, bombs, and petrol bombs. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/04/killed-foiled-attack-saudi-police-station-reports-190421101113605.html (Al Jazeera)]

;Disasters and accidents
*Seventeen people are killed and over a dozen are left missing after a [[landslide]] in the municipality of [[Rosas, Cauca|Rosas]], in southwestern [[Colombia]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/colombia-landslide-1.5106015 (CBC)] [https://www.eltiempo.com/colombia/cali/drama-por-deslizamiento-que-arraso-viviendas-en-rosas-cauca-351816 (El Tiempo)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Ukrainian presidential election]]
**According to exit polls, comedian  [[Volodymyr Zelensky]] wins Ukraine's presidential run-off election over incumbent [[President of Ukraine|President]] [[Petro Poroshenko]] with more than 70 percent of the votes. Poroshenko concedes defeat. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-ukraine-election/comedian-zelenskiy-wins-ukrainian-presidential-race-by-landslide-exit-poll-idUSKCN1RX01N (Reuters)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-48007487 (BBC)] [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/ukraine-presidential-election-second-round-1.5105896 (CBC)]
*[[2019 North Macedonian presidential election]]
**[[North Macedonia]]ns go to the polls to elect the next [[President of North Macedonia]] in an election dominated by divisions over the [[Prespa agreement]], which resolved the [[Macedonia naming dispute|naming dispute]] between North Macedonia and [[Greece]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-north-macedonia-election/macedonians-vote-in-election-dominated-by-splits-over-name-change-idUSKCN1RX008 (Reuters)]
